Mario Pasik | music = Luis María Serra | cinematography = Eduardo Pinto | editing = Santiago Ricci | distributor = Contracampo | released = {{film date|1998|11||Argentina}} | runtime = 92 minutes | country = [[Argentina]] | language = [[Spanish language|Spanish]] | budget = }} '''''Angel Face''''' ({{langx|es|'''La cara del ángel'''}}) is a 1998 [[Argentina|Argentine]] [[film]], written and directed by [[Pablo Torre (director)|Pablo Torre]]. The film features Virginia Innocenti, Mario Pasik, [[Enrique Pinti]], among others.{{IMDb title|id=0210600|title=La cara de ángel}}. The director, Pablo Torre, dedicated the film to the approximately 30,000 people who "[[Desaparecidos#Operation Condor and Argentina.27s Dirty War|disappeared]]" during Argentina's military dictatorship between 1976 and 1983.{{cn|date=December 2024}} ==Plot== The story takes place during the period of the ruling military ''[[Military junta|junta]]'' in [[Argentina]] from the mid-seventies to the early eighties, focusing on one particular family. The story is told from the viewpoint of Nicolas, a young boy. By mistake the mother of the family is killed by right-wing extremists because they believe she had [[photography|photographed]] a civilian protest march and the violent suppression by a military patrol in Buenos Aires. In fact, her twin sister actually took the pictures. She recognized its leader as the father of her nephew and she shows the pictures to her sister. One day while the sister is out, the man shows up with his political thugs and murders the mother and then hunts for Nicolas who hides inside a large [[Longcase clock|grandfather clock]]. Nicolas (Mario Pasik) is soon taken by his aunt to her home in the country, where he attends the local [[Catholic]] school, where most of the children's parents are in the [[military]]. At the school the [[fascist]] bullies and kids who are frightened by them offer a parallel to Argentina's political situation at the time. The boys imitate their parents with dirty tricks toward a boy they call a ''mixto'' (born from a marriage of [[Jews]] and [[Christians]]) who they regularly beat and torment. Nicolas develops a friendship with the mixto and confides in him about what happened to his mother. A few years later, after the mixto has been taken away, Nicolas and the other bullies take part in the [[Falklands War|Malvinas/Falklands War]]. Afterward, Nicolas settles an old, old score. ==Cast== * Virginia Innocenti * Mario Pasik as Nicolas * [[Enrique Pinti]] * Victor Moll * Mariano Marín * Facundo Garcia ==Background== {{main|Dirty War}} The film is based on the real political events that took place in Argentina after [[Jorge Rafael Videla]]'s reactionary military ''junta'' assumed power on March 24, 1976. During the ''junta's'' rule: the parliament was suspended, unions, political parties and provincial governments were banned, and in what became known as the [[Dirty War]] between 9,000 and 30,000 people deemed left-wing "subversives" disappeared from society.[http://www.yendor.com/vanished/ The Vanished Gallery]. According to the [[Pablo Torre (director)|Pablo Torre]], the producer/director, the film is loosely based on a story written by [[Hans Christian Andersen]]. In his tale, a [[wolf]] wants to eat a family of little [[domestic sheep|lamb]]s. One day, the wolf goes into the house and eats the lambs and the smallest lamb hides in a [[clock]] and then escapes. ''La cara del ángel'' is adapted by Torre for a larger narrative.[http://www.filmfestivals.com/int/overviews/2000/chicago_latino2_00.htm Privett, Ray] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080315092228/http://www.filmfestivals.com/int/overviews/2000/chicago_latino2_00.htm |date=2008-03-15 }}. Interview with [[Pablo Torre (director)|Pablo Torre]] at the [[Chicago Latino Film Festival]], March 31, 2000. ==Critical reception== ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' magazine film critic Howard Feinstein, reporting from the Puerto Rico Film Festival, gave the drama a mixed review, writing, "Once again, an Argentine pic attempts to probe the national psyche for clues to what fueled the cruel military junta that ruled from 1976 to 1982. ''Angel Face'' is most successful in linking the friendships, fantasies, curiosity and vulgarity of childhood with the workings of the surrounding society. Unfortunately, despite a few fine performances, many of the characters are drawn with a heavy brush, and the direction, photography and editing of this obviously low-budget affair are too uninspired to sustain such a weighty load. Outside of a few Latin American sites, draw will be limited."[https://www.variety.com/review/VE1117913874.html?categoryid=31&cs=1 Feinstein, Howard]. ''Variety,'' film review, March 22, 1999. Last accessed: January 19, 2008. ==Distribution== The film was first presented at the [[Mar del Plata Film Festival]] in November 1998. It was released wide in Argentina on June 24, 1999. The film has been screened at various film festivals, including: the [[Chicago Latino Film Festival]], United States; the [[San Diego Latino Film Festival]], USA; the Puerto Rico Film Festival, and others. ==Awards== '''Wins''' * [[Mar del Plata Film Festival]]: Best Screenplay, Pablo Torre; 1998. ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== * {{IMDb title|id=0210600|title=La cara del ángel}} * {{TCMDb title|id=522092}} * [http://www.cinenacional.com/peliculas/index.php?pelicula=2378 ''La cara del ángel''] at the [[cinenacional.com]] {{in lang|es}} [[Category:1998 films]] [[Category:1998 independent films]] [[Category:1990s political drama films]] [[Category:Argentine drama films]] [[Category:Argentine independent films]] [[Category:Dirty War films]] [[Category:Films about Latin American military dictatorships]] [[Category:1990s Spanish-language films]] [[Category:1998 drama films]] [[Category:Spanish-language drama films]] [[Category:Spanish-language independent films]]
